card.name: Military service and armed forces names
card.fires_on: Words inside or just before references to the armed forces, such as 'service' members, 'U.S. Army', 'Uniformed Services', 'soldiers of', 'joined the Navy', and the Militia. It fires in the middle of the military phrase, before the next military word.

modes.label: Military service law terms
modes.description: Words in names of laws or groups about military service members and veterans.
modes.example: protect the jobs and employer-provided benefits of<< service>> members returning to the civilian workforce, US

modes.label: Army and unit names
modes.description: Words in or right after the names of army units and military bodies.
modes.example: the U.S.<< Army>> Research Laboratory, the U.S. Army

modes.label: Joining or calling up forces
modes.description: Verbs and linking words that lead into a military body being joined or called up.
modes.example: in January 1942 Mr. Smith<< joined>> the Navy.

card.writes: It pushes toward lamp-related words and away from battle and army words, so it seems to damp predictions of combat terms.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a sentence where military service or an armed force is being named.
